description: PART 2c: fix chart UX so every timeframe/range renders a full continuous series like CoinDCX/Delta, default to the 1-minute chart on open, and make the candle chart update in real time tick-by-tick from the BTC live feed (the user's repeated steering: 'chart jo show karega wo bilkul tick by tick chalna chahiye real time me BTC ke according'). This is config + frontend only; it does not change the DB, money math, launch date, or base. Depends on nothing but is best sequenced before FEAT-004/005 because those reuse the same chart plumbing. NOTE: the reported bugs (15m/1W show one-two candles, day view crams years) come from a mismatch between each range's days window and its tf plus insufficient backfill depth for those tfs; the config fix here corrects the windows, and FEAT-004 deepens the backfill that feeds them.
steps: In arv-config.js CHARTS section (~line 335): change defaultTimeframe from '15m' to '1m'. Re-derive the `ranges` array so each range's `days` window and `tf` are matched to produce a readable, populated series (roughly: '1D'->tf '1m' (or '5m'); '1W' days 7 -> tf '15m'; '1M' days 30 -> tf '1h'; '3M' days 90 -> tf '4h'; '1Y' days 365 -> tf '1D'; '5Y' days 1825 -> tf '1D'; 'All' days null -> tf '1W'). Keep defaultRange sensible (e.g. '1D' or '1W' now that default tf is 1m). Ensure the tfs referenced by ranges are all in the `timeframes` array and are all tfs that get backfilled (see next step).

In arv-config.js CHARTS.backfill: ensure every tf used by a range has a backfill depth so the series is not near-empty. Add entries so 5m and 15m are backfilled (e.g. '1m':7, '5m':30, '15m':90, '1h':365, '4h':730, '1D':null, '1W':null). This is the client-declared intent; the server backfill chain is extended in FEAT-004. Keep maxCandles high enough (2600 or raise if a range now needs more bars).

In js/pages/trade.js: the timeframe tabs already start from CFG.CHARTS.defaultTimeframe (st.tf = CFG.CHARTS.defaultTimeframe), so changing the config makes the trade chart open on 1m automatically - verify this and adjust daysFor(tf) so the initial 1m view pulls enough history (e.g. keep 1m->7 days) and so 5m/15m map to windows consistent with the new ranges. Verify the 1m/5m initial visible-range clamp (setVisibleLogicalRange to last ~180 bars) still gives a proper CoinDCX-like zoom.

In js/pages/dashboard.js and js/pages/portfolio.js (from FEAT-002): buildRangeTabs picks CFG.CHARTS.defaultRange from CFG.CHARTS.ranges - confirm the new ranges/defaultRange produce a populated default chart.

IMPLEMENT LIVE TICK-BY-TICK CANDLE UPDATES (the core steering). Currently js/pages/trade.js loads static server candles and only re-polls snapshot every 30s; the live js/feed.js trade stream powers only the nav ticker and tape, never the candle series. Wire the feed into the chart: after loadChart() builds st.series, subscribe via feed.onTick/onTrade (import * as feed from '../feed.js' and call feed.start() once) so each incoming BTC trade updates the CURRENT (latest) candle in real time. Convert the live BTC USD price to an ARV price using the same index relationship the server uses: arvPrice = snapshot.index.base * (btcNowInr / snapshot.index.baseBtcInr), where btcNowInr = feed.priceUsd('BTC') * snapshot.index.fxUsdInr (use the fx and base figures already returned by api.snapshot() in the `index` object: base, baseBtcInr, fxUsdInr). Update the last candle: if the tick falls in the same tf bucket as the last candle, mutate high/low/close and call st.series.update({time, open, high, low, close}); if it starts a new bucket (based on tf_seconds), append a new candle. lightweight-charts' series.update() with the same/greater time performs an in-place last-bar update, which is exactly the grow-tick-by-tick behaviour. Do the same for the area series (update value). Guard for a stale/absent feed so the chart still shows historical candles when the live feed is unreachable.

Apply the SAME live-candle wiring to the ARV performance chart on dashboard.js/portfolio.js if a chart is retained there, so the ARV chart also grows tick-by-tick (the user explicitly wants the ARV chart to be tick-by-tick like Bitcoin). Keep the 30s snapshot poll as the correcting backstop that re-syncs to the authoritative server candle.

Ensure real-time updates respect CFG.FEED.renderThrottleMs coalescing already provided by js/feed.js (feed.onTick is already throttled), so no extra throttling is needed, but avoid rebuilding the whole chart on every tick - only update the last bar.
acceptance_criteria: arv-config.js CHARTS.ranges pairs each range with a tf/days that yields a continuous populated series, and every tf used by a range is present in CHARTS.timeframes and has a CHARTS.backfill depth (5m and 15m included).
Opening the trade chart uses 1m by default (st.tf initialised from CFG.CHARTS.defaultTimeframe) and daysFor() supplies enough 1m history.

js/pages/trade.js imports js/feed.js, starts the feed, and updates the latest candle in place on each live BTC tick (converting BTC->ARV via snapshot.index base/baseBtcInr/fxUsdInr), appending a new candle at each tf-bucket boundary, without rebuilding the chart per tick.
The ARV chart(s) on dashboard.js/portfolio.js (if retained) also update tick-by-tick from the live feed, with the 30s snapshot poll re-syncing to the server candle.
When the live feed is unavailable the chart still renders the historical server candles (no crash).
verification: `node -e "globalThis.window={};require('./arv-config.js');var c=globalThis.ARV_CONFIG.CHARTS;if(c.defaultTimeframe!=='1m')throw'defaultTimeframe not 1m';c.ranges.forEach(function(r){if(c.timeframes.indexOf(r.tf)<0)throw 'range tf '+r.tf+' not in timeframes';});console.log('ok',JSON.stringify(c.ranges),JSON.stringify(c.backfill))"` exits 0 and prints the new ranges/backfill.
`node --check js/pages/trade.js && node --check js/pages/dashboard.js && node --check js/pages/portfolio.js && node --check js/feed.js` reports no parse errors.
`grep -n "feed\.\(onTick\|onTrade\|start\|priceUsd\)\|series.update(" js/pages/trade.js` shows the live-candle wiring is present.

Manual reasoning check (record in findings): confirm the BTC->ARV conversion uses snapshot.index.base and baseBtcInr/fxUsdInr consistently with api/_money.php index_price(), so the live last-bar close matches what the next server candle will store. Cannot be run end-to-end without a live feed; note this.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (config + frontend only; no DB/money-math/base/launch change).

arv-config.js CHARTS: defaultTimeframe '15m'->'1m'; allTimeframe '1D'->'1W'; ranges re-derived so each window pairs with a readable tf: 1D/1m, 1W/15m, 1M/1h, 3M/4h, 1Y/1D, 5Y/1D, All/1W (fixes the '15m/1W show one-two candles' and 'day view crams 5y' bugs, which came from window<->tf mismatch); backfill now covers every tf a range uses: {1m:7,5m:30,15m:90,1h:365,4h:730,1D:null,1W:null} (5m and 15m added per acceptance); maxCandles stays 2600; defaultRange '1Y'->'1W'. Verified with the required node -e config check (exit 0): every range.tf is in timeframes and has a backfill entry, defaultTimeframe==='1m'.

js/pages/trade.js: st.tf already inits from CFG.CHARTS.defaultTimeframe, so the trade chart now opens on 1m automatically. daysFor(tf) adjusted to mirror the new ranges (1m->7, 5m->30, 15m->90, 1h->365, 4h->730, 1D/1W->null) so the initial 1m view pulls a full week of minutes; the existing 1m/5m setVisibleLogicalRange(last ~180 bars) clamp is unchanged and still gives the CoinDCX-like zoom. Added live tick-by-tick wiring: imports `* as feed` and TF_MINUTES from ../feed.js; after loadChart() builds st.series it seeds st.liveBar from the last server candle and subscribes via feed.onTick (feed.start() fired once, fire-and-forget). onLiveTick() computes tf bucket = floor(nowSec/tfSeconds)*tfSeconds; a tick in the same bucket mutates high/low/close, a new bucket appends a fresh candle (open = previous close for continuity); it calls st.series.update({time,open,high,low,close}) for candles or {time,value} for area - only the last bar, never a rebuild. wireLiveFeed() unsubscribes any prior listener first so tf/type switches don't stack listeners. resyncLiveBar() runs inside the existing 30s snapshot poll: it refetches the latest server candle for the current tf and adopts it (only if last.t >= liveBar.t) as the correcting backstop to the authoritative server series.

js/pages/dashboard.js and js/pages/portfolio.js (area charts): same wiring applied - feed import + TF_MINUTES, liveArvPrice(), onLiveTick() updating the area series' last point via st.series.update({time,value}), wireLiveFeed() called at end of loadChart() (idempotent across range switches since the chart/series are reused), and resyncLiveBar() added to the existing 30s poll. buildRangeTabs picks CFG.CHARTS.defaultRange ('1W' -> 15m) which is a populated range.

Guards / fallback: liveArvPrice() returns null when snapshot.index or feed.priceUsd('BTC') is missing/non-finite, so onLiveTick is a no-op and the historical server candles remain on screen; feed.start() is .catch()'d so an unreachable feed never breaks the chart. No extra throttling added - feed.onTick is already coalesced to CFG.FEED.renderThrottleMs (80ms).

MANUAL REASONING CHECK (BTC->ARV conversion vs api/_money.php index_price()): index_price(btcUsd, fx) for quote=INR computes nowQuote = btcUsd*fx, baseQuote = baseUsd*baseFx, returns base*(nowQuote/baseQuote). api/market.php snapshot builds index.baseBtcInr = baseUsd*baseFx (== baseQuote) and index.fxUsdInr = current fx, index.base = arv_base_inr. The client uses price = index.base * ((feed.priceUsd('BTC') * index.fxUsdInr) / index.baseBtcInr) = base * ((btcUsd*fx)/(baseUsd*baseFx)) = base*(nowQuote/baseQuote) - algebraically identical to index_price(), so the live last-bar close matches what the next server 1m candle stores (the server also builds arv candles via index_price on BTC candles). Any small drift between the display-feed BTC price and the server's stored BTC candle is corrected every 30s by resyncLiveBar().

VERIFICATION RUN: `node -e` config check exit 0 (printed new ranges/backfill/defaultRange). `node --check` on trade.js, dashboard.js, portfolio.js, feed.js, arv-config.js all pass (run with `env -u NODE_OPTIONS` per sandbox note). grep confirms feed.onTick/feed.start/feed.priceUsd and series.update() present in all three page modules. No PHP changed, so php -l not required. DEFERRED: no MySQL, no exchange network and no live WebSocket feed in this sandbox, so end-to-end tick growth, backfill depth and the resync backstop cannot be exercised here - they must be validated on a live install. node --check does not resolve imports (../feed.js, ../ui.js, ../api.js), it only checks parse; the import specifiers match existing sibling modules used elsewhere in js/pages.
